description: Stropharia rugosoannulata is a large, robust agaric with a wine-red to reddish-brown cap, gills that mature from pale gray to dark purple-brown, and a distinctive thick, wrinkled (rugose), star-fissured ring on the stem. A vigorous wood-chip saprotroph, it is widely cultivated outdoors as a beginner-friendly edible crop.
edibilityNotes: A choice edible that must be thoroughly cooked; raw or undercooked specimens can cause gastrointestinal upset, and some individuals report sensitivity, so try a small portion first. Confirm the dark purple-brown to blackish spore print and the thick, wrinkled, star-fissured ring before eating. The greatest risk to foragers is misidentification: reddish-brown, ringless or cortina-bearing species in genera such as Cortinarius, Galerina, and Pholiotina can superficially resemble it but produce a rust-brown spore print (not purple-brown to black) and may be deadly poisonous (amatoxins/orellanine). Never rely on cap color alone; always verify the spore print color and the rugose, star-shaped ring.
distribution: Found in temperate regions of the Northern Hemisphere and now widely distributed and cultivated worldwide.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Cortinarius species (webcaps)
dangerousLookalikes.note: Some toxic webcaps, including deadly orellanine-containing species, can be reddish-brown, but they have a cobweb-like cortina rather than a thick rugose ring, produce a rust-brown spore print (not purple-brown to black), and grow as mycorrhizal partners with trees rather than on wood chips.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Galerina marginata (deadly galerina)
dangerousLookalikes.note: A deadly amatoxin-containing species that fruits on wood and can have a brownish cap and a ring zone, but it is far smaller, has a rust-brown spore print rather than purple-brown to black, and lacks the thick star-fissured rugose ring. Confusion is most likely with young or small Stropharia.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Agaricus species
dangerousLookalikes.note: Some Agaricus share a ring and dark gills, but they produce a chocolate-brown spore print, lack the wine-red cap and star-fissured rugose ring, and have free gills with a pink young gill stage; a few Agaricus (e.g. yellow-staining group) cause GI upset.

dangerousLookalikes.name: Pholiotina / Conocybe species
dangerousLookalikes.note: Small brown ringed LBM-type mushrooms that can occur in mulch and lawns; some (e.g. Pholiotina rugosa) contain deadly amatoxins. They are much smaller, slender, and have a rust-brown spore print, unlike the large robust Stropharia with purple-brown to black spores.
